name: Drawdown regime
tagline: De-risking on QQQ's drawdown fails; the one survivor halves the minute stop once QQQ is 8% below its 52-week high.
summary: The mandated overlay - exit to BIL when QQQ is 5/10/15% below its 52-week high - fails on every setting. The 165-day SMA already holds BIL for 80-84% of deep-drawdown sessions, and where the rule does bind, forward TQQQ returns are above average (+11.5% over 20 days in the -8..-12% bucket). The one rule that clears the round-2 bar keeps TQQQ but cuts the intraday stop from 4% to 2% while QQQ is at least 8% below its high: 61.57%/40.34% (10y) and 51.75%/31.63% (5y) at 1 bp, dominating the round-1 winner at 1/5/10 bp.
decision_process: Before each session, QQQ's drawdown from its trailing 252-session high is computed from closes through the prior session, so it is known before the open: dd = QQQ_close(t-1) / max(QQQ_close, t-252..t-1) - 1. The 165-day SMA regime (prior close vs prior SMA) selects TQQQ or BIL. If risk-on and dd <= -8%, the intraday stop is 2% instead of 4%. During the session an armed stop (QQQ first-minute price < prior 20-day SMA x 1.01) exits TQQQ at the next minute's open when the TQQQ close is below session open x (1 - stop); the book stays in BIL for the rest of the session and the night, and re-enters at the next session's open if the regime is still risk-on. Every target set at bar i is filled at bar i+1's open.
rules: Regime: if QQQ's prior daily close is above its 165-day SMA, hold 100% TQQQ including overnight; otherwise hold 100% BIL.
Stop arming: on risk-on sessions only, arm the stop when QQQ's first-minute price is below its prior 20-day SMA times 1.01.

Stop: while armed, if TQQQ's minute close falls more than 4% below the session open (2% when QQQ is at least 8% below its 52-week high), sell at the next minute's open and hold BIL for the rest of the session and the following night.
Re-entry: at the next session's open if the 165-day regime is still risk-on; after a stop the position does not re-enter intraday.
Drawdown definition: QQQ close(t-1) / max(QQQ close, t-252..t-1) - 1, using only completed sessions through t-1.
Long-only, one position at a time, no leverage beyond 100% TQQQ; weights sum to <= 1.
verdict: Strictly dominates the round-1 winner at 1/5/10 bp and has lower drawdown in 82/82 rolling 3-year windows, but the return edge is not statistically significant (20-day block bootstrap p = 0.26), a 2% stop near the high also helps (placebo), and walk-forward parameter selection is neutral-to-worse. The mandated 5/10/15% de-risking gates are a clean negative; two of them even lose to TQQQ buy-and-hold on 10y CAGR.

sources.idea: Conditional stop: halve the minute stop from 4% to 2% while QQQ is at least 8% below its 52-week high.
sources.evidence: Rule came from the round-2 mandate plus this agent's forward-return table: mean 20-day TQQQ return after -8..-12% drawdowns was +11.47% (87% hit rate), so position-level de-risking was rejected and only the stop was tightened. No paper proposes this exact rule.

sources.idea: Fixed drawdown-threshold de-risking cuts volatility and max drawdown but lowers CAGR and does not improve Sharpe/Sortino; losses come from underexposure during recoveries and whipsaws in shallow drawdowns.
sources.source: Strahle, O. (2025) / How Does Reducing Exposure During Drawdowns Impact Portfolio Performance?
sources.evidence: Tests fixed thresholds, linear scaling and moving averages on SPY 2000-2025. All three cut vol and max DD; CAGR fell from 8.03% to 5.27-7.41%; none improved Sharpe or Sortino; Calmar improved only marginally for fixed thresholds (0.18 vs 0.15). The two stated failure modes are exactly the ones measured here.

sources.idea: Drawdown-based rules can reduce risk but change both expected return and risk; there is no free drawdown control.
sources.source: van Hemert, Ganz, Harvey, Rattray, Sanchez Martin & Yawitch (2020) / Drawdowns
sources.evidence: Journal of Portfolio Management paper; abstract and Man Group summary state that drawdown-based rules can be used as a risk-reduction technique but this affects both expected returns and risk. Used to frame the expected trade-off, not to derive a parameter.

sources.idea: Drawdown/dip signals are a momentum-horizon phenomenon: buying weakness at weeks-to-months horizons does not earn reliable alpha, and trend-following protects in prolonged drawdowns.
sources.source: AQR Capital Management (2025) / Hold the Dip (summary by L. Swedroe, Alpha Architect)
sources.evidence: 196 dip-buying rules on the S&P 500, 1965-2025: 60%+ have lower risk-adjusted returns than buy-and-hold, average alpha +0.5%/yr, only 8% significant; during the four worst drawdowns since 2000 dip-buying lost 18.4% vs trend-following +28.6%. Mirrors this agent's finding that selling a drawdown in an intact uptrend fights momentum.

sources.idea: No reliable dip-buying outperformance over passive investing.
sources.source: Bonini, Shohfi & Simaan (2024) / Buy the dip? European Financial Management 30(4)
sources.evidence: Secondary citation for the same mechanism, read only through the Evidence Investor summary of AQR's paper. No parameter or rule taken from it.

sources.idea: Stop-loss rules only add value when returns have positive serial correlation (momentum); otherwise the stopping premium is negative.
sources.source: Kaminski, K. M. & Lo, A. W. (2014) / When do stop-loss rules stop losses? Journal of Financial Markets 18
sources.evidence: The theoretical licence for a stop that is tighter when the market is already in a drawdown (crashes are momentum) and for not using a position-level drawdown exit in ordinary pullbacks (which mean-revert). The 2%/4% split is this agent's implementation, not the paper's.

sources.idea: A drawdown constraint is costly insurance: optimal drawdown control trades expected return for a smaller maximum loss.
sources.source: Grossman, S. J. & Zhou, Z. (1993) / Optimal investment strategies for controlling drawdowns. Mathematical Finance 3(3)
sources.evidence: Standard theory reference for why a drawdown floor lowers expected growth. Not used to calibrate anything; reported as framing only.

sources.idea: Drawdown can be constrained/optimised as a risk measure (CDaR), which formalises the return-versus-drawdown trade-off.
sources.source: Chekhlov, A., Uryasev, S. & Zabarankin, M. (2005) / Portfolio optimization with drawdown constraints
sources.evidence: Background on drawdown-constrained optimisation. No rule or parameter taken from it.

sources.idea: Hold a risky asset only while it is above its long moving average; otherwise hold cash. This is the base 165-day SMA regime inherited from the round-1 winner.
sources.source: Faber, M. T. (2007) / A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation
sources.evidence: The 10-month/200-day time-series trend rule family. The 165-day SMA and the TQQQ/BIL implementation are the round-1 winner's, not Faber's; Faber supplies the prior, not the parameter.

sources.idea: Base rules and benchmark: 165-day QQQ SMA regime, 4% armed minute stop, 58.80%/44.56% (10y) and 49.88%/33.49% (5y) at 1 bp.
sources.evidence: Internal round-1 winner record. This agent reproduced it exactly (657/337 fills, 58.7979%/44.5647% and 49.8752%/33.4905%) before adding any drawdown rule.

rejected_sources.source: Mandate rule: full exit to BIL when QQQ is 5% / 10% / 15% below its 52-week high, re-enter at -2% / -5% / -10%
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Tested. 1 bp results: -5% gate 25.43%/48.18% (10y) and 10.02%/48.18% (5y); -10% gate 35.52%/55.92% and 31.17%/43.20%; -15% gate 56.27%/44.56% and 45.25%/33.49%. The -10% gate is worse on drawdown than the winner, and the -5% and -10% gates fall below TQQQ buy-and-hold's 39.28% 10y CAGR. The 165-day SMA already holds BIL for 80-84% of deep-drawdown sessions.

rejected_sources.source: Underwater-duration exit: 100% BIL after 120 sessions with no new 52-week high
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Tested. 52.56%/49.04% (10y) and 40.90%/33.49% (5y) at 1 bp: lower CAGR and a worse 10y drawdown than the winner.

rejected_sources.source: De-lever to QQQ (beta 1) while QQQ is at least 8% below its 52-week high
rejected_sources.why_rejected: Tested. 45.58%/42.48% (10y) and 37.85%/32.82% (5y) at 1 bp: the drawdown falls less than the return, failing both round-2 targets.

Tested as a control. 53.15%/43.77% (10y) and 37.95%/43.77% (5y) at 1 bp. Much worse than conditioning the tight stop, so the drawdown state is doing real work, but the 5y drawdown is far worse than the winner's 33.49%.

rejected_sources.source: Moreira & Muir (2017) / Volatility-Managed Portfolios; Cederburg, O'Doherty, Wang & Yan (2020) / On the Performance of Volatility-Managed Portfolios
rejected_sources.why_rejected: These papers appear on the current web card but were never used by this agent and no volatility-targeting rule was tested here. They belong to the round-1 drawdown-stop-overlay agent's V4 volatility-target variant. Mis-attribution.

corrections: FACTUAL: the report and web page say 'Against TQQQ buy-and-hold ... every variant in the table passes, including the failing drawdown overlays.' That is false. dd05_bil (10y CAGR 25.43%) and dd10_bil (35.52%) both fall below TQQQ's 39.28% 10y CAGR; only their drawdowns are lower. Corrected in report.md section 7; the web page must be regenerated.

STATUS: the card says 'Alternative'. It should be 'Fragile': the rule formally dominates, but the return edge is inside noise (block-bootstrap p = 0.26), a placebo (2% stop when QQQ is within 5% of its high) also improves the result, and walk-forward parameter selection is neutral-to-worse.

ATTRIBUTION: remove Moreira & Muir (2017) and Cederburg et al. (2020) from the card's papers list; they were never used by this agent (they belong to drawdown-stop-overlay's volatility-target variant). Add Kaminski & Lo (2014), which is the actual theoretical support for the surviving conditional-stop rule.

RULES: replace 'Base: round-1 winner.' and 'Other drawdown thresholds were rejected.' with the real rules (165-day SMA vs prior close, BIL otherwise, MA20 x 1.01 arming, 4% stop and 2% when QQQ dd <= -8%, next-minute-open fill, out overnight). 'Other thresholds were rejected' is a research finding, not a trading rule.

METRICS: the card reports only 1 bp. Add 5 bp: 56.78% / 43.23% (10y) and 47.29% / 32.39% (5y). Do not present the 1 bp numbers without the cost label; the 10 bp row is 51.00% / 46.64% and 41.89% / 33.35%.

BENCHMARK: the page uses TQQQ 39.28% / 81.68% (README bar). The harness's own 1-minute benchmark from the window start is 39.38% / 82.29% (10y) and 14.29% / 82.29% (5y). Either label the README numbers as the bar or add the harness values.
